identity.name: Grönefeld 1941 Remontoire

case.material: stainless steel (also in titanium, rose gold)

identity.one_liner: The 1941 Remontoire is the Grönefeld brothers' signature — a hand-finished in-house movement with an 8-second constant-force remontoire, in a 40mm steel case that is the most-cited modern Dutch independent watch.

narrative.story: The Grönefeld brothers (Tim and Bart) are third-generation watchmakers from Oldenzaal, Netherlands, who established their brand in 2008. The 1941 Remontoire is the watch that put them on the global map: a 40mm steel case containing an in-house manual-wind movement with an 8-second remontoire — a constant-force mechanism that re-tensions the mainspring every 8 seconds, dramatically improving rate stability. The 1941 is named after the brothers' grandfather, who was a horology instructor in 1941. Production is roughly 12 pieces per year. The 1941 is the most-cited modern Dutch independent watch in international collector circles.
narrative.collector_notes: The 8-second remontoire uses a small auxiliary spring that is wound and released every 8 seconds, providing a constant force to the escapement. The main plate of the movement is hand-finished with a "frosted" texture that takes roughly 4 hours per movement. Production is roughly 12 pieces per year. The brand is among the most-awarded independents of the past decade.
